meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Acabou o seu tempo is the standard phrase for 'Your time is up.'
Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Used as a noun (o brasileiro = the Brazilian citizen) or as a nationality adjective.

examples.text: Você falou o que o brasileiro queria ouvir.
examples.trans: You said what the Brazilian wanted to hear.

examples.text: O povo brasileiro é muito criativo.
examples.trans: The Brazilian people are very creative.

meanings.note: Followed by an infinitive for your own wish (quero saber) or que + subjunctive for someone else (quero que você entre).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

meanings.note: Irregular first-person present eu ouço; past eu ouvi.
Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Você já sabe o que quer comer?
examples.trans: Do you already know what you want to eat?
We ate very well at that restaurant.

meanings.note: Dead body; plural cadáveres.

examples.text: Pro cadáver eu gosto de usar esse.
examples.trans: For the corpse I like to use this one.

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Describes both tasty food and pleasant sensations like um calor gostoso (a lovely warmth).

examples.trans: What pleasant warmth at the beach!

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: O recado das urnas is a journalistic cliché for the message sent by voters at the polls.

examples.text: Esse foi o recado das urnas.
examples.trans: That was the message from the ballot boxes.
I left a message for you.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
In Brazilian elections, as urnas refers to the electronic voting machines and the overall vote count.

examples.trans: The ballot boxes have already been counted.

examples.text: Esse foi o recado das urnas.
examples.trans: That was the message from the ballot boxes.

meanings.note: Covers knowing facts or finding out information.

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: Superlative-strength everyday word for 'great'.
Used standalone as a one-word question and confirmation: Acordo? — Acordo. (Deal? — Deal.).

examples.trans: Do we have a deal then?

meanings.note: Limits a statement (eu só quero) or forms só que (except that / the catch is).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

examples.text: Só que agora ela precisa de ajuda.

meanings.note: Passar impune means to go unpunished; passar por means to undergo.

examples.text: Eles passam por muitos testes lá.
examples.trans: They go through many tests there.

meanings.note: Informal reduced para. Before a feminine noun, this Brazilian spelling can also represent a contraction including the article a; the exact meeting is clear from context.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Passar numa faculdade pública means to pass the entrance exam for a tuition-free public university.

examples.trans: You got into a public university.

meanings.note: Modifies nouns like segurança pública (public safety).

examples.text: Essa é minha proposta pra segurança pública.
examples.trans: That is my proposal for public safety.

meanings.note: Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?
examples.trans: Do you think you're better than us?
Oh, folks, the meeting ran late.

meanings.note: Used in O que está acontecendo? (What is going on?) and O que aconteceu foi que... (What happened was that...).
Often reinforced with é que in questions (como é que foi?).

examples.text: Como é que foi a cirurgia?
Como é que tá meu marido?

meanings.note: Possessive determiner agreeing with the possessed noun; in Brazil it most often means your (with você).

examples.text: É isso que você quer pra sua vida?
examples.trans: Is that what you want for your life?

meanings.note: O seu pedido foi realizado means your wish/request was granted.
O seu pedido foi realizado means your wish has been granted.
Contraction of em + uma before a feminine singular noun.

examples.trans: I work on a good team.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.
Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: Marks the current moment resulting from an earlier action.

examples.trans: Now she is in a meeting.

examples.text: Agora tenho que resolver umas coisinhas.
examples.trans: Right now I have to sort out a few little things.

meanings.note: Você vai ter que estudar means You are going to have to study.

examples.text: Você vai ter que estudar muito.
examples.trans: You are going to have to study a lot.
She studies at a public university.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).
Time between midday and evening; boa tarde! greets or bids farewell in the afternoon.

examples.text: A reunião é hoje à tarde.
